## ✨ Novidades
- 🎮 **Remapear o controle pela interface** — abra **Controller Config → Buttons** e rebinde **A / B / X / Y / Start / Z**, gatilhos e D-pad direto na tela; **"Restaurar padrões"** volta ao layout GameCube. (Antes a tela ficava presa tentando ler um teclado inexistente — por isso não deixava mudar os botões.) O mapeamento é salvo e persiste entre boots.
- 🖼️ **Texturas persistem entre sessões** — habilitou o texture pack uma vez e ele carrega **sozinho** em todo boot; acabou o "precisar reativar na mão" toda vez que reabria o jogo.
- 🎮 **Layout de ombros estilo GameCube** — o **Z** do GameCube agora fica no **bumper R**, e o **−** passa a ser **exclusivo do menu** (não vaza mais um "Z" no jogo ao fechar o menu). Padrão: GC L = ZL, GC R = ZR. Não gostou? Agora dá pra remapear.
- 💾 **Menos desgaste do SD** ao mexer nos sliders de configuração (as gravações são agrupadas em vez de uma por passo).

(Previously the screen was stuck waiting for a non-existent keyboard, which is why buttons couldn't be changed.) Your mapping is saved and persists across boots.
- 🖼️ **Texture packs persist across sessions** — enable your texture pack once and it loads **automatically** on every boot; no more re-toggling it each time you reopen the game.
- 🎮 **GameCube-style shoulder layout** — GameCube **Z** now lives on the **R bumper**, and **−** is **menu-only** (it no longer leaks a "Z" into the game when you close the menu). Defaults: GC L = ZL, GC R = ZR. Don't like it? You can remap it now.
- 💾 **Less SD wear** when adjusting settings sliders (writes are batched instead of one per step).

packages.changelog: --- - Purchase your copy on [GOG](https://www.gog.com/en/game/fallout) or [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/38400/). The files need to be from a Windows installation. - Download the latest [release](https://github.com/ryandeering/fallout-ce-switch/releases/latest) or build from the source. See YAML pipelines for reference. - Drag the installation files into a new folder called `fallout1` in your `switch` folder on the root of your SD card. You can also put `fallout1` on the root of your SD card. - Put the necessary executable in your `switch` folder on the root of your SD card, either `.nro` or `.nso`. ## Changes compared to previous release ### Performance & stability - Faster loading. Art assets are pre-cached at startup, so maps, saves and area transitions load quicker. Note that initial load will be a bit longer. I would expect less stutter if any also. - Runtime diagnostics overlay. Press L+R+Right Stick Click for live FPS, frame time, memory usage and startup load timing. More a curio than useful to average person using this, but at least you can tell me if there's bad framerate somewhere! ### Controls - **L shoulder button now toggles active item, to stop using the cursor to do it. Should make switching items much, much smoother.** - Pressing the left stick now opens the native keyboard when a text input field is present. Otherwise, it's stealth mode. - No more accidental double-triggers on menus, inventory, the Skilldex and quick save/load. ### Native keyboard - Character names, save names and search dialogs all use the Switch software keyboard, sorry about this not being included on initial release. - Item quantity dialogs use a dedicated numeric keypad instead of increment and decrement buttons. - The "Ask About" dialog for dialogue with NPCs opens the keyboard automatically. ### Save compatibility - Save files from the PC version of Fallout 1 CE generally work on Switch now, and Switch saves work back on PC. Some heavily modded or unusual saves may still fail to load. **This is experimental.** - Make backups before moving saves between platforms. ### Setup and configuration - `fallout1_nx.ini` is created automatically on first launch with sensible defaults. - Introduced `fallout1` fallback folder on root of SD card, like the Fallout 2 port. [Fallout 2 port that I've also worked on. (similar QOL updates soon!)](https://github.com/ryandeering/fallout2-ce-switch/releases/latest) Thank you for your patience and enjoy. ## How Many Dudes? NX v1.0.0

The first public release of the unofficial **How Many Dudes? Android wrapper for Nintendo Switch**.

This port runs the original Android ARM64 GameMaker runner natively through a lightweight Android/JNI compatibility layer.

### Features

- Fully playable gameplay
- Touch-screen controls
- ASTC texture rendering
- Native audio playback
- In-game cutscene support
- Local saves and preferences
- Suspend and resume support
- Optimized performance during high-unit-count battles
- Automatic handheld and docked resolutions
- Built-in crash and performance logging

### Controls

This game is designed around tapping, dragging, and direct unit placement. Therefore, this port intentionally uses the Nintendo Switch touch screen.

**Handheld mode is required for practical gameplay.** Joy-Con and Pro Controller controls are not currently supported.

### Installation

This release does not include any copyrighted game files.

You need a legally obtained Android ARM64 APK of **How Many Dudes?**, specifically build `100.0.890` (`com.bscotch.hmd`).

From the APK, extract:

- `lib/arm64-v8a/libyoyo.so`
- The complete `assets/` folder
- The APK itself, renamed to `game.apk`

Place everything on your SD card as follows:

```text
sdmc:/switch/hmd_nx/
├── hmd_nx.nro
├── libyoyo.so
├── game.apk
└── assets/
    ├── game.droid
    └── ...
```

Launch the Homebrew Menu using a full title override by holding **R** while opening an installed game. Applet/Album mode is not supported.

See the repository README for automatic Windows setup and complete instructions.

### Limitations

- Google Play Games, cloud saves, achievements, billing, ads, and Android in-app updates are unavailable.
- Other APK versions may use a different GameMaker runner and are not guaranteed to work.
- Controller input is not implemented.

### NRO Checksum

SHA-256:

```text
8CA8DFF643C3AC9DFA97C9710887459E23ED035E6C016F71A1FC9F3C14E45EA0
```

### Legal

This is an unofficial compatibility wrapper. No APK, game code, `libyoyo.so`, `game.droid`, or other original asset is included.

**How Many Dudes?** and its assets belong to Butterscotch Shenanigans and their respective rightsholders. Users must obtain the original game legally.

## Changes
* fix the Y button.

## Installation and running
Unzip the attached ZIP file into the `switch` folder on your SD card.

If you already have an OpenMW install on your PC:
1. Copy your `openmw.cfg` into `/switch/openmw/config/` (for Windows users: it's in `Documents/My Games/OpenMW`).
2. Copy your data files (esm, esp, bsa) into `/switch/openmw/data/`.

If you don't, but you own Morrowind:
1. Install Morrowind.
2. Copy the `Data Files` folder and `Morrowind.ini` file from your Morrowind installation into `/switch/openmw/data/`.

Then run OpenMW from hbmenu.

## Known issues
* Exiting the game using the HOME button during a loading screen will crash it.
* Cursor sometimes displays when it shouldn't.
* Performance isn't very good.
* User accounts that have non-ASCII characters in the name will be treated as an absence of user account (i.e. your saves will go into `global`).

## Notes
* You **have** to run this from either NSP hbmenu or from a game override. Applet mode does not offer enough memory.
* Press MINUS to bring up the software keyboard when an input field is selected.
* Click LSTICK to enable/disable gamepad cursor control.
* This has only been tested with the English release of Morrowind GOTY Edition. Mods should probably work, however you'll have to either edit your `openmw.cfg` manually or use openmw-launcher on PC, then copy the config file over.
* If the game crashes, check `/switch/openmw/fatal.log` and `/switch/openmw/config/openmw.log`.

First release of the Sonic Triple Trouble 16-Bit wrapper for the Nintendo Switch. The game is fully playable from start to finish at a locked 60 FPS.

**What Works**

1. **Fully Playable:** The game can be completed from start to finish without crashes.
2. **Locked 60 FPS**: Native ARM64 execution with no emulation layer. The GMS2 runner runs directly on Switch hardware at full clock speed.
3. **Full Controller Support:** All physical buttons are mapped — A, B, X, Y, D-Pad (all 4 directions), both analog sticks, +, −, L, R, ZL, ZR. D-Pad support was implemented via reverse-engineered GameMaker's internal Hat event system (onGPNativeHat) rather than raw key codes.

6. **Save Data:** Game progress and settings persist correctly. Saves are flushed safely on exit and when the application is backgrounded.
7. **Performance:** Optimized with -O3 -ffast-math, extended CPU boost window for asset loading, and a larger SDL2 audio buffer to minimize callback overhead and frame time spikes.

# The Minish Cap — Nintendo Switch (native homebrew) · USA + PT‑BR

Native **Nintendo Switch** homebrew builds of the Minish Cap PC‑decompilation port — a **native recompilation** (it runs on the Switch's own CPU with a software PPU/APU; **it is not an emulator**). Two builds:

- 🇺🇸 **USA** — original English.
- 🇧🇷 **BR (PT‑BR)** — Brazilian Portuguese translation (*romsportugues* "T1.0‑Final") + Portuguese overlay UI by default.

> ⚠️ **No game data is included.** The `.nro` ships only the engine + a pre‑baked asset cache. You must provide your **own legally‑dumped GBA ROM** — it supplies the actual game data.

## ✨ What's included in these builds
- 🏆 **RetroAchievements** — full `rcheevos` / `rc_client` integration over HTTPS, with a styled in‑game unlock overlay (issue #12).
- ⚡ **GPU renderer (OpenGL ES 2)** — runs **60 fps without overclocking**.
- 🎮 **Controls** — A/B mapped to Nintendo's physical face‑button layout, analog‑stick support.
- 🔤 **On‑screen menu** — scaled overlay/settings (Minus button), FPS‑counter options, multilingual (EN / PT / ES).
- 📂 **Loads any `*.gba` by content**, not by filename — so a translation hack works as‑is.
- 🛠️ Opt‑in frame profiler; clean RELEASE build (no per‑frame SD logging).

---

## ✅ Requirements
- A Nintendo Switch with custom firmware (**Atmosphère**) and the **Homebrew Menu** (hbmenu).
- The **matching GBA ROM** for the build you want (table below).

## 💾 Required ROM per build (check the SHA‑1!)

| Build | ROM you need | SHA‑1 of the ROM |
|---|---|---|
| **USA** | The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap (USA) | `b4bd50e4131b027c334547b4524e2dbbd4227130` |
| **BR / PT‑BR** | Minish Cap PT‑BR translation — *romsportugues T1.0‑Final* | `6838e0405c1be5d867d84e019d1f131a366b07ad` |

Verify yours before copying: `sha1sum your_rom.gba`. It must match **exactly** or the game won't load correctly.

## 📥 Installation — where & how
1. On your SD card, create the folder **`/switch/tmc/`**.
2. Copy **your ROM** into it, renamed to exactly **`baserom.gba`** → so you end up with **`/switch/tmc/baserom.gba`**.
   - USA build → put the **USA** ROM here. · BR build → put the **PT‑BR hack** ROM here.
3. Copy the downloaded **`.nro`** to **`/switch/`** (any subfolder works; hbmenu scans recursively).
4. On the Switch, open the **Homebrew Menu** and launch the `.nro`.
5. First launch builds the asset cache (a few seconds) and the game starts.

> ⚠️ **One ROM at a time.** Both builds read `/switch/tmc/baserom.gba`. To switch between USA and BR, replace `baserom.gba` with the matching ROM **and delete the folder `/switch/tmc/assets/`** so the cache rebuilds for the new ROM.

- The BR build is the proven USA engine running the translation's assets — there is no separate "EU" build here (the genuine European BZMP cart isn't supported yet).
- `.nro` download hashes (SHA‑256), to verify your download:
